sections.h2: Who sends and collects a Warren County tax bill?
sections.html:
Warren County divides the job three ways, and all three offices answer calls on weekdays. One office values the house, a second sends the bill and takes payment, and a third picks up any balance left on April 15.

  • PVA: 429 E. 10th Avenue, Bowling Green, KY 42101, phone (270) 843-3268 per the county's department list, open 8:00 to 4:30.
  • Sheriff: (270) 842-1633, with a tax inquiry page for looking up and paying a bill. Its business office keeps the same 8:00 to 4:30 hours.
  • County Clerk: P.O. Box 478, Bowling Green, KY 42102, phone (270) 842-9416. The clerk's own site sends property tax and valuation questions to the PVA.

The sheriff's page grounds the office's collector role in KRS 134.140 and 160.500, and says it passes the money on to each state, county, school and district authority.

sections.h2: What does the sheriff's 2026 payment schedule look like?
sections.html:
The sheriff's site laid out the 2026 dates and told owners to expect a bill in the first week of October. Each stage tracks the state calendar in KRS 134.015.

  • October 1 to November 1, 2026: 2 percent off.
  • November 2 to December 31, 2026: the amount on the bill.
  • January 2027: 5 percent more.
  • February 1 to April 15, 2027: a 21 percent charge that bundles the 10 percent penalty with the sheriff's fee.

The 2026 discount window closed November 1, 2026. Paying online carries a cost: $1.50 for a card payment of $60.00 or less, 2.49 percent above that, and $1.50 per ACH or e-check payment. American Express is refused. The site refreshes after 7:00 pm on business days, so a Friday payment may not appear until Monday night. On a large bill, an ACH payment avoids the percentage.

sections.h2: Why do two Warren County neighbors pay different rates?
sections.html:
Warren County has two public school districts. Warren County Public Schools serves the county and the outlying parts of Bowling Green, and Bowling Green Independent Schools serves most of the city proper. The clerk's 2025 rate sheet shows how big that choice is: a city school levy of 84.80 cents against 52.20 cents for the county district.

Warren County 2025 real estate levies, cents per $100 of assessed value (County Clerk rate sheet)

State10.60

Library3.70
Public health2.90
Extension and conservation0.85

School, county district52.20
School, city district84.80

The county levies add to 21.45 cents. Adding the pieces yields three combined rates: 84.25 for land outside any city, 104.55 for city land in the county school district, and 137.15 for city land in the city school district. Ask the sheriff which combination your address pays.

sections.h2: What would the median Warren County house owe?
sections.html:
QuickFacts lists $258,000 as the midpoint home value. Assuming an assessment at that figure, the three combined rates produce annual bills of roughly $2,173.65 in the unincorporated county, $2,697.39 in a city with county schools, and $3,538.47 in a city with its own school district. The gap of more than $1,300 between the first and the last is something a buyer will notice.

Assessments and sale prices rarely match, so treat these figures as a way to compare districts. A homeowner who qualifies for the $49,100 exemption pays on $208,900 instead, which saves about $413.67 a year at the 84.25 rate.

sections.h2: Who gets the homestead exemption in Warren County?
sections.html:
Claims go to the PVA from owners who are 65 and over or who count as totally disabled. The deduction is $49,100 for each of 2025 and 2026, and a birth certificate, license or passport backs up the age claim. The QuickFacts count of residents who are 65 or older is 14.2 percent.

A disability claim comes up for yearly renewal. Two groups never renew: service disabled veterans, and owners whom Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems rated permanently and totally disabled.

sections.h2: How do I contest a Warren County value?
sections.html:
Book a conference with the PVA at the number in the county directory, (270) 843-3268, since state rules make it the first step. Viewing of the roll lasts thirteen days, beginning the first Monday in May. A taxpayer who has met with the PVA then files at the County Clerk before the day after inspection ends.

  • Photos, insurance records, building costs and sales listings are the evidence the local board expects.
  • Anyone paid to speak for you must be a professional such as an attorney, accountant, appraiser or broker, and must carry written authority.
  • Hearings start 25 to 35 days after viewing ends and run no more than five days.

Written reasons accompany any decision to raise or lower a value.

sections.h2: What does the Warren County Clerk do with bills unpaid on April 15?
sections.html:
At the close of that day, the sheriff sends over every open bill as a certificate of delinquency carrying a lien. The clerk keeps accepting payment right up to the annual sale and publishes a PDF list of current delinquent parcels. For 2026 the clerk scheduled the sale at 9:00 am on August 26 in Suite 100 at 429 E 10th Ave, with buyer registration due August 17. Both dates have passed.

After the transfer, costs layer on quickly. The meter runs at 1 percent monthly. The clerk's commission is 10 percent of tax, penalty and interest, and the county attorney adds 20 percent unless the bill is paid within five business days. A $10 lien recording and release fee also applies. Because the lien clings to the land for up to eleven years, sellers should pay it off at closing and get a release from the clerk.

sections.h2: What else should a Warren County seller know about the county?
sections.html:
Warren was carved from Logan County in 1796 and is Kentucky's fifth most populous county, with Bowling Green as its seat. Barren River runs through the city, with the Green River marking the north edge. Interstate 65 and the Natcher Parkway (renamed I-165 in 2019), turned a farming county into a manufacturing one in the 1960s and 1970s. Cities besides Bowling Green are Oakland, Plum Springs, Smiths Grove and Woodburn. Visitors know it for Western Kentucky University, Beech Bend Park, the Corvette assembly plant and the National Corvette Museum.

Census QuickFacts shows the growth: 149,375 people in mid 2025, with 1,453 building permits issued during the year. Rent at the median is $1,002 a month, and 55.6 percent of homes are lived in by owners. Among adults, 32.3 percent have a bachelor's degree, and 10.4 percent of residents were born outside the country.

Permits matter. The county's Division for Building Services, at 1141 State Street, covers everywhere except Bowling Green and Oakland, charges $0.15 per square foot with a $45 minimum, and sets a fine of at least $500 for work begun without a permit. Sheds from 120 square feet and all pools need one. Phone (270) 843-5360 to ask about a past project before you list.

faqs.q: Which office takes payment for Warren County property tax?
faqs.a: The Warren County Sheriff's Office takes it, at (270) 842-1633. Use the tax inquiry page on its website to look up and pay a bill.

faqs.q: Did the 2026 Warren County discount end?
faqs.a: Yes. The window was October 1 to November 1, 2026. After that the face amount stands until December 31, 2026, and January 2027 adds 5 percent.

faqs.q: Why is the Warren County school tax higher in some places?
faqs.a: The city school district levy is 84.80 cents per $100, against 52.20 cents for the county district, according to the clerk's 2025 rate sheet. Parcels inside the city's own district pay the higher one.

faqs.q: Does Warren County charge extra to pay by card?
faqs.a: Yes. Card payments run $1.50 up to $60.00 and 2.49 percent over that. ACH and e-check payments cost $1.50, and American Express is not accepted.

faqs.q: What is the population of Warren County?
faqs.a: The Census estimate is 149,375 for July 2025. That is 11.0 percent above the April 2020 base of 134,563, and the clerk's own website calls the county the fastest growing in Kentucky.
